intro: Rotate PDF straightens pages that were scanned sideways or upside down and turns wide plans and tables to landscape. The rotation is stored as a property of each page, just like when you rotate and save in a PDF reader, so text, images and links stay intact and the file size barely changes.

Pick the rotation (90° clockwise, 90° counterclockwise or 180°) and the pages it applies to. All pages is the default; you can also type a range such as “1-3, 8”, or “even” and “odd”, which helps when a duplex scanner leaves every back page upside down.

If each page needs something different, open “More options” and use “Rotation per page” with page:degrees pairs separated by commas, for example “2:90, 5:180, 7:-90”. On those pages that value overrides the general rotation. Rotation adds to whatever the page already had, so turning it 90° twice leaves it upside down.

Everything happens in your browser: the PDF is never uploaded to a server. You can choose several files and they are all rotated with the same settings; afterwards you download them one by one or in a ZIP.

faq.a: No. Nothing is redrawn or recompressed: only the orientation each page is shown in changes.

faq.q: Does it detect the right orientation by itself?
faq.a: No: you say which pages to turn and by how much. If you are not sure which ones are crooked, open the file in the PDF reader first and look through the thumbnails.

faq.q: Can I use any angle in the per-page rotation?
faq.a: Only multiples of 90°, such as 90, 180, 270 or -90. With any other value the tool warns you and does not create the file.

faq.q: My PDF has a password. Can I rotate it?
faq.a: Yes. The page asks for the open password and the file is opened in your browser; the password is not sent anywhere.
